recipes.name: Palak Dal (Spinach Lentil Curry)
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is rich in fiber from lentils and spinach, which helps lower LDL cholesterol. Spinach also provides vitamins and antioxidants, supporting overall heart health. Lentils are a good source of plant-based protein.
instructions: Wash and soak Toor Dal for 20 minutes. Drain and pressure cook with 2 cups water, turmeric powder, and salt for 3-4 whistles.
In a separate pan, heat mustard oil. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter.
Add chopped onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and mushy. Stir in coriander powder.
Add chopped spinach and cook until it wilts completely.
Add the cooked dal to the spinach mixture. Add remaining water if needed to adjust consistency. Bring to a simmer for 5-7 minutes.
Serve hot with brown rice or whole wheat roti.

recipes.name: Hariyali Fish Tikka (Grilled Fish with Mint Chutney Marinade)
recipes.health_benefit: Fatty fish like salmon or rohu are excellent sources of Omega-3 fatty acids and Vitamin D, both crucial for cardiovascular health and overall well-being. Grilling minimizes added fats, making it a heart-healthy protein choice.
instructions: Blend mint leaves, coriander leaves, green chilies, ginger, garlic, lemon juice, cumin powder, garam masala, and salt into a smooth paste.
In a bowl, mix the fish cubes with the low-fat yogurt and the prepared green paste. Ensure fish is well coated. Marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Preheat grill or oven to medium-high heat (200°C/400°F).
Thread the marinated fish onto skewers. Brush lightly with mustard oil.
Grill for 8-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until the fish is cooked through and lightly charred. Alternatively, bake in the oven for 10-15 minutes.
Serve hot with a squeeze of fresh lemon and a side salad.

recipes.name: Oats Upma with Vegetables
recipes.health_benefit: Oats are a soluble fiber powerhouse, proven to help lower LDL cholesterol. The addition of various vegetables boosts fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making this a wholesome and heart-healthy breakfast.
instructions: Dry roast oats in a pan for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Set aside.
In the same pan, heat mustard oil. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter. Add curry leaves, green chili, and grated ginger.
Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. Add mixed vegetables and cook for 3-5 minutes until slightly tender.
Stir in turmeric powder and salt. Add water and bring to a boil.
Gradually add the roasted oats, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, until all water is absorbed and oats are cooked.
Garnish with roasted peanuts (if using) and serve hot.

recipes.name: Mixed Vegetable Brown Rice Pulao
recipes.health_benefit: Brown rice provides complex carbohydrates and more fiber than white rice, contributing to better cholesterol management. The abundance of vegetables adds essential vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

ingredients.item: Mixed Vegetables (Carrots, Green Beans, Peas, Cauliflower)

instructions: Wash brown rice thoroughly and soak for at least 30 minutes. Drain well.
In a large pot or pressure cooker, heat mustard oil. Add cumin seeds, bay leaf, and cinnamon stick. Sauté until fragrant.
Add sliced onion and sauté until golden brown. Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for 1 minute.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add the chopped mixed vegetables and sauté for 3-5 minutes.
Add the soaked brown rice, salt, and water. Stir well. Bring to a boil.
If using a pot, cover and simmer on low heat for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked and water is absorbed. If using a pressure cooker, cook for 3-4 whistles.
Let it rest for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with Raita (low-fat yogurt based).

recipes.name: Lean Chicken Chettinad
recipes.health_benefit: Lean chicken breast provides high-quality protein without excessive saturated fat, supporting muscle maintenance. The spices used in Chettinad cuisine have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, contributing to overall health.
instructions: Marinate chicken with half of the ginger-garlic paste, salt, and lemon juice for 30 minutes.

For the spice paste: Dry roast all whole spices (coriander to cinnamon) until fragrant. Add grated coconut and roast for another minute. Let cool and grind to a fine powder with a little water to make a paste.
In a large pan, heat mustard oil. Add curry leaves, green chilies, and remaining ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chopped onion and cook until golden brown.
Add the chicken and cook until it changes color.
Stir in the prepared Chettinad spice paste and tomato puree. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring well, until the raw smell disappears and oil starts to separate.
Add water, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Serve hot with whole wheat roti or brown rice.

recipes.name: Fortified Low-Fat Yogurt with Berries and Flaxseeds
recipes.health_benefit: Low-fat yogurt, especially if fortified, can contribute to Vitamin D intake and provides calcium and probiotics. Berries are rich in antioxidants and fiber, while flaxseeds offer Omega-3 fatty acids, all beneficial for heart health.
instructions: Pour low-fat yogurt into a bowl.
Top with mixed berries.
Sprinkle ground flaxseeds over the berries.
Add a drizzle of honey if desired for sweetness.
Enjoy immediately.

recipes.name: Besan Cheela with Vegetables and Tomato Chutney
recipes.health_benefit: Besan (chickpea flour) is a good source of plant-based protein and fiber, promoting satiety and supporting healthy cholesterol levels. The vegetables enhance nutrient density and fiber content.
instructions: For Cheela: In a bowl, whisk besan with water to form a smooth, lump-free batter of pouring consistency. Add chopped onion, bell pepper, green chili, coriander leaves, turmeric powder, cumin powder, and salt. Mix well.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over medium heat. Lightly grease with mustard oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it evenly in a circular motion to form a thin pancake. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.
Cook until the edges turn golden brown and the cheela is cooked through. Flip and cook the other side. Repeat for remaining batter.
For Chutney: In a small pan, heat 0.5 tsp mustard oil. Add cumin seeds and dried red chili. Sauté for a few seconds.
Add chopped tomatoes and garlic. Cook until tomatoes soften. Let cool, then blend into a smooth chutney with salt.
Serve hot cheelas with fresh tomato chutney.

Manage stress through practices like meditation, deep breathing exercises, or hobbies, as chronic stress can negatively impact cardiovascular health.
Stay well-hydrated by drinking plenty of water throughout the day.
Avoid smoking and limit alcohol consumption, as these can negatively impact heart health and overall well-being.
